Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and rollout evidence, then use the required fish-control bookshelf plus the wake-visual inspection skill before proposing the single candidate. I’ll keep implementation-specific reasoning in the requested log and ensure the reusable guidance is evidence-backed.

The workspace contract confirms the prefilled solver is the assigned parent, formal CFD is off-limits, and the candidate must remain materializable throughout. I’m now loading the complete required skill instructions and inherited guidance before inspecting all sampled scores, trajectories, and keyframes.

The sampled set contains no failed rollout: every available sheet is a target-reaching finite trajectory. I’ll therefore compare the best sampled success with the most informative regressed success, while using the inherited quantitative failure lessons only as boundary evidence. This is the closest evidence-complete comparison available without inventing a failure case.

The wake sheets show a coherent, self-propelled diagonal route in both comparisons; the measurable difference is confined to the late correction, not wake entry or base propulsion. Following the required bookshelf protocol, I’m now consulting mechanism primitives for a compact state-feedback refinement that preserves the traveling wave and avoids scalar-only tuning.

The bookshelf points to a terminal “yaw/slip-aware approach” mechanism. The inherited branch also provides a useful negative boundary: replacing total body speed with positive range closure slightly regressed the same scaffold, so I will not repeat denominator tuning. I’m reading the shelf’s source notes for the response-gated redirect and path-following families before translating only their invariant.

The selected candidate will keep the parent’s full gait and gates unchanged, and change only terminal route prediction: as the distance/body-speed cap shortens the look-ahead, steering will smoothly blend from instantaneous yaw projection toward the observed windowed bearing trend. That adds measured slip/course response without a signed wake-force guess or a new route threshold.

The pre-edit notes are recorded, and the single solver candidate now contains only that terminal course/slip-aware prediction change. I’m updating the durable experience bank with the supported lesson from the parent replay and the matched closing-speed regression; I will not claim the new candidate’s unevaluated behavior as evidence.

Verification is now following the required check-runner contract: first the semantic guidance/provenance guard, then the Julia policy contract, then the solver boundary check. No CFD rollout will be run.

The semantic guard passed. The Julia check could not start because `julia` is absent from the current PATH (the policy itself did not fail); I’m checking the workspace’s configured Julia location and will rerun the contract if a local runtime is available.

The boundary check passed, confirming only the allowed solver file changed. No Julia runtime is installed in this environment, so I’m completing the remaining static review—schema references, finite bounded branches, file diffs, and provenance consistency—and will report the runtime-check limitation explicitly.

Static review is clean: all required files are non-empty, the candidate differs from the parent only in the bounded terminal prediction block, the guidance change is substantive, and no whitespace/conflict markers were found. The two runnable required checks pass; the Julia-only check remains unavailable because no Julia executable exists anywhere in the configured system locations.

Implemented exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:67) adds bounded terminal course/slip-aware bearing prediction while preserving the parent gait.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:3) contains the visual diagnosis, hypothesis, falsification boundary, and bookshelf transfer record.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:170) adds the evidence-backed terminal look-ahead lesson and negative denominator-tuning result.

Checks: guidance guard passed; solver boundary passed; static schema/file/conflict checks passed. The Julia contract command could not run because Julia is not installed. No CFD was run.
